verdicts.reason: A puts the CTA button at the very top, above the book and the headline, so the reading order is reversed. The book floats without its circle backdrop, the circle drifts to the bottom right where the subhead runs into its edge, and the bottom third is dead space. B keeps the original order (headline, copy, CTA, fine print) but just spreads it down the canvas with big uniform gaps. Its book sits off-centre on the circle's top edge and the fine print is tiny, but it reads correctly.

A has a strong book-left, text-right composition, but the CTA is shrunk to a small pill above the headline, which weakens it and reverses the reading order. The whole group sits in the top 60% with the lower 40% empty, and the text column runs into the edge of the detached circle. B (the same as pair 1's B) keeps the right hierarchy and a prominent CTA, but its gaps are loose and stretched and the book is misaligned with the circle.
